answer: A pairwise vouching bond makes every new identity enter through a single narrow inlet: an established agent must stake tokens as a lantern vouching for the newcomer, and both stakes are slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. A Sybil attacker therefore cannot spawn identities freely - each one costs a real sponsor bond and reputation, and a comet of fake accounts would burn the sponsor stake the moment the first fraud is exposed. The bond decays as the newcomer builds its own verified work history, so honest agents graduate to independence while attackers pay full price for every clone.
